newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas soy harvest gets under way in week.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas soy harvest gets under way in week.

text.p: Harvest of soybeans got under way in Arkansas with seven days suitable for field work in the week ended on August 25, the state agricultural statistics service said.
Soybeans were two percent harvested as of Sunday, against nil last year and against the five-year average. Soybeans were rated 56 percent good to excellent and 29 percent fair.
Corn harvest progressed to 18 percent complete from 11 last week, 24 last year and 29 on average. Corn was rated 72 percent good to excellent, up one percentage point.

Sorghum was 16 percent harvested against 11 last week, nil last year, and eight percent average. The crop was rated 34 percent mature against 22 y/a, 41 avge. Condition was rated 51 percent good to excellent, unchanged from last week.
Rice was five percent harvested, against three last week, nil last year and five average. The crop was rated 81 percent good to excellent.

Cotton continued to suffer from boolworm and weevil in some counties but the crop was still rated 71 percent good to excellent, against 72 pct last week. Sixteen percent of the crop had opened bolls from 10 w/a, 19 y/a and 10 avge.
Topsoil moisture was rated 16 pct very short, 38 short, 43 adequate and three surplus -- a decline from the week earlier.
